summary: Round 4, everything re-measured by mutation in a review tree at the staged bytes (baseline :format:test :sequencer:test :ingest:test BUILD SUCCESSFUL). BOTH ROUND-3 SURVIVORS ARE DEAD AS CLAIMED: (a) `if (count <= 0 || count > c.remaining())` -> `if (count == 0)` at CommitDelta.java:214 now FAILS anOverLargeSegmentCountIsREFUSEDNotAllocated with `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Requested array size exceeds VM limit` (5 tests completed, 1 failed); (b) reverting the podId read to `c.bytes((int) c.uvarint())` FAILS anOverLongPodIdOrIncarnationLengthIsREFUSED; (c) deleting `incLen < 0 ||` at Checkpoint.java:324 now FAILS :format:test, and the parallel `podLen < 0 ||` at :315 is also pinned. EVERY EARLIER MAJOR IS STILL DEAD, re-measured this round: pre-ADR-0036 merge lambda at CheckpointWriter.java:154-157 -> BUILD FAILED; `pointerEpoch=0; pointerSequence=0` at :150-151 -> BUILD FAILED (tr-1, tr-2, r2-1); `version != VERSION && version != VERSION_ATTRIBUTED` -> `version > VERSION_ATTRIBUTED` -> BUILD FAILED (tr-3); deleting all three PodState invariants -> BUILD FAILED (tr-4); deleting CommitRequest's requireNonNull+isBlank on incarnationId -> BUILD FAILED (tr-5). Two SPEC-named risks are also dead: the PARTIAL HOIST (podId per segment, incarnation and flushSeq taken from segment 0) -> BUILD FAILED; minting the incarnation per FLUSH in DefaultIngest.java:355 -> BUILD FAILED. Swapping epoch/sequence on the wire -> BUILD FAILED. RED RECORDS ARE HONEST: all five AttributedDeltaTest ids are re-recorded at 2026-09-07T10:31:31-10:32:04 and the edited CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest#anOverLongIncarnationLengthIsREFUSEDRatherThanNarrowed at 10:32:06; tdd_scan binds each record to the METHOD-BODY hash of the staged blob (not the file), so check-tdd passing means the recorded reds are the bytes being committed -- and I independently measured that each of those tests DOES fail under its corresponding mutation, so the reds were earnable rather than fabricated. THE ANSWER TO THE DELETED-TEST QUESTION IS NO: the `count <= 0` half HAS an observable consequence and the javadoc that now records otherwise is a measurement that is false. Two further guard halves in the same new helper are untested. Three majors below.

findings.title: The deleted test's reasoning does not hold, and its replacement javadoc records a false measurement: `count <= 0` IS observable, and dropping it lets an OutOfMemoryError escape `throws IOException` -- the exact defect the test beside it exists to pin.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED in a review tree at the staged bytes. The javadoc at AttributedDeltaTest.java:115-122 asserts the `count <= 0` half 'needs no case of its own' because 'a negative count narrows to 4, the loop then runs zero times, and CommitDelta's empty-delta guard refuses the object anyway'. That is true only of the value chosen. MUTATION: `if (count <= 0 || count > c.remaining())` at CommitDelta.java:214 -> `if (count > c.remaining())` -- dropping ONLY the sign half. :format:test :sequencer:test :ingest:test is BUILD SUCCESSFUL (exit 0). I then measured the harm with a throwaway test in the tree: splice the uvarint of 0xFFFFFFFF_7FFFFFFF (bytes FF FF FF FF F7 FF FF FF FF 01) over the segment-count byte of a one-segment attributed delta. That value is NEGATIVE as a long, so `count > c.remaining()` is false, and it narrows to Integer.MAX_VALUE. MUTATED: `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Requested array size exceeds VM limit` out of `new ArrayList<>((int) count)` at CommitDelta.java:219, straight past CommitDelta.decode's `throws IOException` and every `catch (IOException)` ChainReplay and a recovering leader have -- verbatim the escape anOverLargeSegmentCountIsREFUSEDNotAllocated exists to prevent, reached by the OTHER half of the same predicate. UNMUTATED: the same bytes are refused as IOException and the throwaway test passes (BUILD SUCCESSFUL). So the test the author deleted is earnable: it needs a negative count whose LOW 32 BITS ARE A LARGE POSITIVE INT, not one narrowing to 4. A value narrowing to a small int is caught downstream by the empty-delta guard and proves nothing -- exactly the trap the author already documented one level up for the Checkpoint incLen case and then fell into here. Two harms, not one: the guard half is unpinned, and the javadoc now tells the next session, in as many words, that it cannot be pinned.
findings.surviving_mutation: CommitDelta.java:214 -- `if (count <= 0 || count > c.remaining())` becomes `if (count > c.remaining())`. Full :format:test :sequencer:test :ingest:test stays BUILD SUCCESSFUL, and a KIND_DELTA_ATTRIBUTED entry whose segment count is the uvarint 0xFFFFFFFF_7FFFFFFF then throws OutOfMemoryError instead of IOException.

findings.title: `anOverLongPodIdOrIncarnationLengthIsREFUSED` names both fields and splices only podId; the incarnationId bound is deletable with the full build green, and the mutant ACCEPTS a corrupt object.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED in a review tree at the staged bytes. The test builds a one-segment fixture and searches for the length prefix of "poda" only; nothing in the tree splices the incarnationId prefix on the KIND_DELTA_ATTRIBUTED path. MUTATION: revert CommitDelta.java:228-229 to the pre-fix form `String inc = new String(c.bytes((int) c.uvarint()), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);`, leaving the podId bound in place. :format:test :sequencer:test :ingest:test is BUILD SUCCESSFUL (exit 0). Harm measured with a throwaway test: encode `new CommitDelta(9, [SegmentCommit("seg/a", 1 run, Attribution("poda", "inc-1", 4))])`, find the incarnation length prefix (value 5, followed by 'i','n','c') at offset 42, and splice the uvarint of 0x1_0000_0005 (85 80 80 80 10) over it -- a value that narrows to 5, the CORRECT length, so the rest of the object parses to the end. MUTATED: decode ACCEPTS and returns `CommitDelta[sequence=9, segments=[SegmentCommit[segmentKey=seg/a, ..., attribution=Attribution[podId=poda, incarnationId=inc-1, flushSeq=4]]]]` as though the bytes were conforming. UNMUTATED: `java.io.IOException: a delta claims a 4294967301-byte incarnationId but only 6 bytes remain`. The incarnationId is the field ADR-0036 adds and the one M4.10d will key dedup on; the test that claims to cover it covers the sibling. Fix is one more splice in the same test, red-first.
findings.surviving_mutation: CommitDelta.java:228-229 -- `attributionLen(c, "incarnationId")` becomes `(int) c.uvarint()`. Full :format:test :sequencer:test :ingest:test stays BUILD SUCCESSFUL, and an attributed delta whose incarnationId length is the uvarint 0x1_0000_0005 is ACCEPTED instead of refused.

findings.title: The new `attributionLen` helper reproduces the SAME `< 0` hole the author just closed in Checkpoint this round, and no test pins it for either field: the mutant ACCEPTS a corrupt object.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED in a review tree at the staged bytes. This round added `negativeNarrowingToThree` to CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest to pin `incLen < 0` in Checkpoint.java:324 -- and the identical predicate in the NEW helper CommitDelta.java:204 got only the positive-wide case (the test splices 0x1_0000_0004, which is positive). MUTATION: `if (len < 0 || len > c.remaining())` at CommitDelta.java:204 -> `if (len > c.remaining())`. :format:test :sequencer:test :ingest:test is BUILD SUCCESSFUL (exit 0). Harm measured with a throwaway test: splice the uvarint of 0xFFFFFFFF_00000004 (bytes 84 80 80 80 F0 FF FF FF FF 01) over the "poda" length prefix -- NEGATIVE as a long, so `> c.remaining()` is false, and it narrows to 4, the CORRECT length. MUTATED: decode ACCEPTS and returns `Attribution[podId=poda, incarnationId=inc-1, flushSeq=4]`. UNMUTATED: `java.io.IOException: a delta claims a -4294967292-byte podId but only 11 bytes remain`. The same mutation on the incarnationId field survives for the same reason. This is a strictly analogous miss to the one the round-3 note says was found and fixed on the checkpoint side: the fix was applied to Checkpoint and copied into a new helper in CommitDelta without its test coming along. The remedy is the value the author already worked out one file over -- reuse it against both attribution fields.
findings.surviving_mutation: CommitDelta.java:204 -- `if (len < 0 || len > c.remaining())` becomes `if (len > c.remaining())`. Full :format:test :sequencer:test :ingest:test stays BUILD SUCCESSFUL, and an attributed delta whose podId (or incarnationId) length is the uvarint 0xFFFFFFFF_00000004 is ACCEPTED instead of refused.

findings.title: The backlog row says the pod slot is 'decoded from an ENUMERATED {0,1}'; the flag is read as `== 1` and nothing pins a value outside that set.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED in a review tree at the staged bytes. MUTATION: `if (version == VERSION_ATTRIBUTED && c.uvarint() == 1)` at Checkpoint.java:322 -> `... && c.uvarint() != 0`. :format:test :sequencer:test :ingest:test is BUILD SUCCESSFUL (exit 0). No test in CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest or CheckpointPodStateTest splices the presence flag with a value other than 0 or 1, so the enumerated domain the row names is neither implemented nor asserted: production silently reads a flag of 2 as ABSENT and continues, rather than refusing it. I could not construct a case where such an object is fully ACCEPTED -- with the fixtures available the misalignment always trips the trailing-bytes check at Checkpoint.java:335 -- which is why this is minor rather than major: the mutation survives, but on well-formed input the two forms are equivalent and on corrupt input both are refused, just for the wrong reason. Recording it because the criterion's word is 'ENUMERATED' and the surviving mutation shows nothing holds the decoder to it.
findings.surviving_mutation: Checkpoint.java:322 -- `c.uvarint() == 1` becomes `c.uvarint() != 0`. Full :format:test :sequencer:test :ingest:test stays BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
